positions.name: OwnedIntelligenceVersusRentedSubstrate
positions.frame: When substrate is treated as a commodity, where does the retained value actually sit — in what is rented, or in what is kept as perspective?
positions.why: Both expressions perform the same antithetical maxim — owned/rented in src-2, commodity/asset in src-3 — using matched technical vocabulary cast as a balanced, unhedged opposition (register's AphoristicTechnicalMaxim, style's CommodityVersusAssetAntithesis, conviction's CategoricalDistinctionAsBedrock, and value's OwnershipAsValueDistinction all converge on exactly these two segments). The directional reads agree closely enough — same register, same flat calm-positive delivery, same principle-level conviction — that they name one locus rather than two: the question of where value is retained once the substrate is commoditized. No existing strata or narrative leaf was supplied to home this under, so it is left unplaced.

The supplied graph structure and strata are both empty, so no existing leaf or category can hold this; the perspective's own map and focus section confirm no prior coverage of owned/rented intelligence or substrate-as-commodity framing exists to reuse. The position pass already found these two segments converge on one locus across register, style, value, and conviction reads, supporting a single leaf rather than two.
